edges.effect_quant: Mostly mechanistic and preclinical work suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.mechanism: The interaction hypothesis is that genotype changes how the exposure is handled or translated into downstream biology, whether through lipoprotein trafficking, one-carbon metabolism, appetite regulation, or lactose-related dietary behavior. For Chronic systemic inflammation, that means any observed effect should be read as effect modification, not genetic destiny.
edges.summary: Interaction studies tend to be directionally interesting but smaller and less stable than mainstream single-exposure associations. Mostly mechanistic and preclinical work link apoe4 with omega-3 exposure to lower chronic systemic inflammation in ApoE4 carriers. The average effect is usually unknown rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
